  • Eyerman, Journal of Transpersonal Psychology (2020)
  • Brewerton et al., Journal of Trauma & Dissociation (2022)
Then (1985) — The Emperor Wears No Clothes

The Endocannabinoid System Discovery: Herer Was Right About the Biology

Herer argued that cannabis was not a recreational intoxicant but a substance with profound biological significance — documented medical utility across hundreds of conditions over thousands of years. He could not explain the biological mechanism, only document the historical evidence.
confirmed
Raphael Mechoulam and colleagues at Hebrew University identified the first endocannabinoid, anandamide (arachidonoylethanolamide), in 1992. This established that the human body produces its own cannabinoid-like compounds and has specific receptor systems designed to respond to them. CB1 receptors (primarily in the brain and central nervous system) and CB2 receptors (primarily in the immune system) are distributed throughout the body in patterns that explain the broad therapeutic relevance Herer documented. The endocannabinoid system regulates: pain, mood, appetite, memory, immune function, and stress response. Herer's claim that cannabis had extensive medical utility was biologically grounded in a receptor system that wasn't discovered until seven years after his book was published.

Sources

  • Devane et al., Science (1992) — anandamide discovery
  • Mechoulam & Parker, Annual Review of Psychology (2013)
Then (1985) — The Emperor Wears No Clothes

The $40 Billion Cannabis Industry: Who Benefits?

Herer's vision of legalization was implicitly community-centered: small farmers, local dispensaries, community-controlled production. He imagined that the cannabis economy would benefit the communities most harmed by prohibition — particularly Black and Latino communities disproportionately targeted by enforcement.
contested
The legal cannabis industry is approximately $40 billion annually in the US (2024). Market concentration: the five largest multistate operators (MSOs) control approximately 20% of licensed revenue. Venture capital investment: $4.2 billion in 2021 (down from peak). The racial equity gap: Black Americans own approximately 4% of cannabis businesses. Social equity license holders have faced systemic barriers — access to capital, banking restrictions under federal law, regulatory compliance costs — that favor well-capitalized applicants over community members most harmed by prohibition. Cannabis remains the fastest-growing industry in America; its growth has not transferred economic value to the communities Herer was writing about.

Sources

  • MJBizDaily, Cannabis Industry Report (2024)
  • Marijuana Policy Project, Social Equity Scorecard (2024)
  • ACLU, Racial Equity in Cannabis (2023)
Then (1985) — The Emperor Wears No Clothes

The Agronomic Claim: Hemp vs. Cotton

Herer argued that hemp fiber was superior to cotton in yield, water efficiency, and pesticide requirements — that if hemp were legalized, it would displace cotton as the dominant textile fiber in America.
confirmed
Agronomic comparisons (USDA Agricultural Research Service, 2021): hemp produces comparable fiber yield to cotton per acre with approximately 50% less water and minimal pesticide requirement. Hemp's protein content, omega fatty acid profile, and soil impact are superior to cotton's across multiple metrics. The commercial reality: textile cotton's supply chain is deeply embedded — gin infrastructure, fiber processing, spinning, dyeing — representing a century of investment that hemp fiber cannot quickly displace. Patagonia and Levi's have introduced hemp-cotton blend fabrics; these represent a small fraction of their production. Hemp fabric as a percentage of US textile consumption is below 1% as of 2026. The agronomic case is confirmed; the commercial transition is far slower than Herer predicted.

Sources

  • USDA Agricultural Research Service hemp studies (2021)
  • Patagonia hemp product development reports
  • Hemp Business Journal market analysis (2024)
Then (1985) — The Emperor Wears No Clothes

The Federal Banking Problem: How Prohibition Persists Without Scheduling

Herer focused on the Controlled Substances Act as the primary mechanism of prohibition. He did not anticipate that even after state legalization, federal banking law would create a secondary prohibition: cannabis businesses cannot access FDIC-insured banks, cannot take card payments, cannot access SBA loans, cannot deduct business expenses (280E), cannot go public on US stock exchanges.
contested
The SAFE Banking Act (Secure and Fair Enforcement for Banking Act) passed the House seven times between 2019 and 2023 and repeatedly failed in the Senate. As of June 2026, cannabis businesses in legal states still cannot access federal banking services. This means: all-cash operations (security risk); inability to pay federal taxes by check; no credit card processing; no SBA financing; 280E federal tax (paying taxes on gross revenue, not profit, creating 70-90% effective tax rates). The federal banking exclusion is now the primary mechanism of cannabis prohibition — more practically significant than the CSA scheduling itself for legal-state businesses. Herer identified the CSA as the problem; the banking problem is the residual wall that his book did not anticipate.

Sources

  • American Bankers Association cannabis banking report (2024)
  • SAFE Banking Act legislative history
  • 280E tax analysis, CannaAdvisors (2024)
Then (1985) — The Emperor Wears No Clothes

The Medicinal Cannabis Science: From Historical Claims to Clinical Evidence

Herer documented historical medical uses of cannabis extensively — 19th century pharmacopeia listings, physician testimonials, pre-prohibition clinical accounts. He was arguing from historical evidence in the absence of controlled trials. The controlled trial evidence was largely prohibited by scheduling.
confirmed
The clinical evidence for medical cannabis has developed significantly since legalization enabled research. Strongest evidence (multiple RCTs): chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (FDA-approved synthetic THC since 1985); chronic pain (systematic review of 28 RCTs, Aviram & Samuelly, 2017 — positive); spasticity in multiple sclerosis (Collin et al., RCT, 2007 — positive); childhood epilepsy syndromes (Epidiolex, FDA-approved 2018 — the first cannabis-derived FDA drug). Moderate evidence: anxiety, insomnia, PTSD (symptom management). Limited evidence: cancer-direct treatment (anti-tumor in vitro; no Phase 3 trials). Herer's historical evidence has been partially confirmed by controlled trials; his broader claims about cancer treatment remain at pre-clinical stage.

Sources

  • Aviram & Samuelly, Pain Physician (2017)
  • Epidiolex FDA approval and clinical data (2018)
  • National Academies of Sciences, Health Effects of Cannabis (2017)
Then (1993) — True Hallucinations

The Entity Research Program: From Anecdote to Survey Science

McKenna described machine elves as a consistent phenomenon of DMT experience, encountered across thousands of independent reports he had collected through lectures and correspondence. He had no systematic data — only his own experience and what audiences told him. His claim was phenomenological: something consistent is happening.
partially-confirmed
Davis et al. (J. Psychopharmacol. 34(9):1008-1020, 2020, Johns Hopkins, n=2,561 people who had already had an entity encounter): entities described as 'beings of light,' 'elves,' 'aliens,' 'guides,' 'angels'; 78% rated entities as conscious and intelligent; 72% believed entities existed 'in their own right'; 80% described lasting positive effects on well-being. A 2021 Frontiers in Psychology EEG study with n=39 is often cited here for an entity-contact-specific neural signature; no such paper exists, and no published study has isolated one. Timmermann et al. (PNAS 120(13), 2023, EEG-fMRI): global functional connectivity rose sharply and network segregation broke down; the study did not isolate entity contact. McKenna's anecdotal observation is now a documented, survey-measured phenomenon; it is not yet neurally characterised.

Sources

  • Sexton et al., J. Psychopharmacol. 33(9) (2019)
  • Timmermann et al., PNAS 120(13) (2023)
  • Lawrence et al., Scientific Reports 12:8562 (2022)
  • Davis et al., J. Psychopharmacol. 34(9):1008-1020 (2020)
Then (1993) — True Hallucinations

Dennis McKenna's Scientific Career: What La Chorrera Built

Terence treated Dennis as the scientific grounding of the La Chorrera expedition — the botanist who would provide the empirical anchor for the speculative cosmological work. Dennis was 19 years old at La Chorrera. Terence could not have predicted what Dennis's career would become.
partially-confirmed
Dennis McKenna went on to: PhD in botanical sciences from UBC (1984); postdoctoral research at Stanford; co-founder of the Heffter Research Institute (1993, which funded some of the earliest Johns Hopkins psilocybin research); research scientist at Aveda and Shaman Pharmaceuticals; Senior Lecturer at the University of Minnesota; co-author of the first pharmacological description of ayahuasca's MAO inhibition mechanism (McKenna et al., 1984). His ayahuasca pharmacology papers are foundational in the field. The Heffter Institute he co-founded funded Roland Griffiths's psilocybin safety study (2001) — which launched the modern research renaissance. La Chorrera sent Dennis into pharmacological botany; his career built the institutional infrastructure that produced the psychedelic research renaissance.

Sources

  • McKenna et al., Journal of Ethnopharmacology (1984) — ayahuasca MAO mechanism
  • Heffter Research Institute founding documents (1993)
  • Griffiths et al., Psychopharmacology (2006)
Then (1993) — True Hallucinations

The Endogenous DMT Confirmation: Is the Spirit Molecule Really There?

Strassman's hypothesis — that the pineal gland produces elevated DMT at key life transitions — was circulating in the psychedelic community before True Hallucinations was published. McKenna was aware of it and incorporated it into his worldview. Both McKenna and Strassman believed that endogenous DMT was a key to consciousness, dreaming, and near-death experience.
partially-confirmed
Barker et al. (Psychopharmacology, 2012): confirmed DMT presence in human blood, urine, and cerebrospinal fluid under ordinary conditions. The enzymes for DMT synthesis (INMT, AADC) are present in the brain, lung, and other tissues. Dean et al. (Scientific Reports, 2019): identified elevated DMT synthesis in rat brains under cardiac arrest conditions — consistent with the near-death experience hypothesis. The pineal gland-specific hypothesis: the pineal has the enzymatic machinery but no study has demonstrated that it produces elevated DMT at near-death, during sleep, or at birth in concentrations sufficient for psychedelic effect. Endogenous DMT exists. Its biological role remains unclear. Strassman's specific pineal-at-key-moments hypothesis is unconfirmed.

Sources

  • Barker et al., Psychopharmacology (2012)
  • Dean et al., Scientific Reports (2019)
  • Yanakieva et al., Journal of Psychopharmacology (2019)
Then (2000) — True Hallucinations

Psychedelic Science After McKenna: Does the Field Engage His Questions?

McKenna died in 2000, before the research renaissance. His questions — about entity contact, plant consciousness, the combinatorial problem — were outside the scope of mainstream research in his lifetime. True Hallucinations ended with the 1971 experience; the research program that would address his questions was decades away.
partially-confirmed
The Psychedelic Science 2023 conference (Denver, 12,000+ attendees) included dedicated symposia on: DMT entity contact (multiple papers, including Timmermann 2023); plant consciousness and ayahuasca pharmacology; the Stoned Ape hypothesis revisited; the combinatorial problem in ethnobotany. McKenna's specific questions are now research programs. The Johns Hopkins Center for Psychedelic and Consciousness Research explicitly includes 'plant-human relationships' and 'entity contact phenomenology' in its research agenda. The combinatorial problem remains open but is being engaged by ethnopharmacologists with modern analytical tools. The questions McKenna died asking are being asked in peer-reviewed journals in 2026.

Sources

  • Psychedelic Science 2023 Program
  • Johns Hopkins Center for Psychedelic Research agenda
  • Timmermann et al., PNAS 120(13) (2023)
Then (2000) — True Hallucinations

The Rhetorical Legacy: What McKenna's Voice Did to the Movement

McKenna's primary medium was the spoken lecture — he gave hundreds of talks from the mid-1980s until his death. The recordings, widely circulated on the early internet and then on streaming platforms, have been heard by tens of millions of people. His rhetorical style — confident, witty, encyclopedic, willing to say outrageous things — was unlike any other psychedelic advocate.
partially-confirmed
McKenna's lecture recordings are among the most-streamed psychedelic content on YouTube and podcast platforms — millions of plays on individual lectures decades after his death. The Joe Rogan-McKenna connection (Rogan has cited McKenna as a primary influence) routes McKenna's ideas through the largest podcast audience in English-language media. Graham Hancock, Duncan Trussell, Paul Stamets, and others in the popular psychedelic space credit McKenna as foundational. The stoned ape hypothesis, the machine elves, the archaic revival, the dominator culture — these enter mainstream discourse through McKenna's rhetorical construction, amplified through podcast culture. The scientific community's engagement with these ideas is partly a response to how widely McKenna's framing has spread.

Sources

  • YouTube McKenna lecture analytics
  • Joe Rogan Experience, McKenna retrospective episodes
  • Psychedelic media landscape survey, Chacruna Institute (2023)
Then (1998) — The Cosmic Serpent

Mycorrhizal Networks: Forest Intelligence Confirmed

Narby's methodological argument — that Western science underestimated plant intelligence by assuming passivity rather than investigating it — was his most important contribution. He had no empirical proof of forest-scale communication; he was calling for investigation.
confirmed
The mycorrhizal network research (Simard et al., Nature, 1997 — published simultaneously with Narby's book; Finding the Mother Tree, 2021) demonstrated: trees transfer carbon, water, and nutrients to kin seedlings through fungal networks; 'mother trees' recognize and preferentially support their offspring; the network responds to damage signals, allowing neighboring trees to increase defensive chemical production. Gagliano's plant learning research (Oecologia, 2014; Nature Plants, 2016) demonstrated associative learning and memory in plants without neural systems. The Plant Signaling & Behavior journal (founded 2006) publishes hundreds of papers annually on plant cognition. Narby's specific biophoton hypothesis is unconfirmed. His methodological prediction — that investigating plant intelligence would find it — has been confirmed on every scale from cellular to forest.

Sources

  • Simard et al., Nature (1997)
  • Gagliano et al., Oecologia (2014)
  • Plant Signaling & Behavior journal, 2006-2026
Then (1998) — The Cosmic Serpent

The UNDRIP Framework: Indigenous Knowledge Rights in International Law

Narby argued that indigenous pharmacological knowledge was intellectual property that could not be appropriated without consent and benefit-sharing. This was a moral argument in 1998, grounded in examples of biopiracy (the ayahuasca patent case). There was no international legal framework that enforced it.
contested
UNDRIP (United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, 2007): Articles 11 and 31 affirm indigenous peoples' rights to their cultural heritage, traditional knowledge, and cultural expressions. The Nagoya Protocol (2010, entered into force 2014): requires prior informed consent from indigenous and local communities before accessing biological resources and associated traditional knowledge; mandates benefit-sharing agreements. 143 parties as of 2026. Enforcement: uneven. The psychedelic pharmaceutical industry largely does not comply with Nagoya's spirit: no company developing psilocybin, MDMA, ibogaine, or ayahuasca derivatives has publicly documented PIC from the indigenous communities whose knowledge pointed toward these compounds. The framework exists; it is not enforced in the domain Narby cared most about.

Sources

  • UNDRIP Articles 11, 31 (2007)
  • Nagoya Protocol status report (2025)
  • Chacruna Institute, Indigenous reciprocity in psychedelic research (2024)
Then (1998) — The Cosmic Serpent

Ayahuasca Clinical Trials: The Medicine Narby Described Is Now FDA-Tracked

Narby's account of ayahuasca's healing properties — anti-parasitic, antidepressant, addiction treatment, trauma resolution — was based on ethnographic observation and early naturalistic studies. No RCTs existed in 1998.
confirmed
Palhano-Fontes et al. (Psychological Medicine, 2019): first RCT of ayahuasca for depression, n=29, significant reduction in MADRS score at Day 7 (p<0.001). Dos Santos et al. (Psychopharmacology, 2016): systematic review of 28 studies, consistent antidepressant and anti-anxiety effects. Hamill et al. (Frontiers in Psychiatry, 2019): meta-analysis of observational studies, positive findings across depression, anxiety, PTSD, substance use. The specific anti-parasitic properties of plants in the ayahuasca brew: Callaway & Grob (Journal of Ethnopharmacology, 1998) documented anti-helminthic activity. Multiple investigational new drug (IND) applications for ayahuasca are filed with the FDA as of 2026. The medicine Narby documented in 1998 has a Phase 2 RCT, multiple systematic reviews, and an IND pathway.

Sources

  • Palhano-Fontes et al., Psychological Medicine (2019)
  • Hamill et al., Frontiers in Psychiatry (2019)
  • FDA IND filings for ayahuasca (2024-2026)
Then (1998) — The Cosmic Serpent

The Decolonization of Psychedelic Research: Narby's Framework Applied

Narby's central argument was that Western science appropriated indigenous knowledge without acknowledgment, credit, or benefit-sharing. He was describing a historical pattern. He did not predict a political movement that would organize around this critique.
partially-confirmed
The 'decolonization of psychedelics' discourse has become a significant force in the psychedelic research community since approximately 2018. Key organizations: Chacruna Institute for Psychedelic Plant Medicines (Beatriz Caiuby Labate, founded 2017) explicitly addresses indigenous reciprocity; Zendo Project incorporates indigenous ceremony acknowledgment into its harm reduction model; MAPS's Indigenous Reciprocity Initiative acknowledges that MDMA-AT builds on knowledge traditions using MDMA-like plant compounds. Psychedelic Science 2023 included multiple panels on decolonization, indigenous rights, and benefit-sharing. Several major research papers now include acknowledgment of indigenous knowledge origins. No major pharmaceutical company has implemented a Nagoya-compliant benefit-sharing agreement for psychedelic compounds. The discourse has reached the center of the field; implementation lags significantly.

Sources

  • Chacruna Institute publications (2017-2026)
  • MAPS Indigenous Reciprocity Initiative
  • Psychedelic Science 2023 decolonization panels
Then (1998) — The Cosmic Serpent

The DNA Biophoton Hypothesis: Has Anyone Tested It?

Narby proposed a specific mechanism: DNA biophoton emissions, amplified by DMT's enhancement of visual processing, provide the information channel through which shamans access molecular-level pharmacological knowledge. This is the testable core of the hypothesis.
contested
As of June 2026, no published study has directly tested the biophoton-DMT mechanism Narby proposed. Biophoton research has continued: Popp's group has established that DNA does emit biophotons in the visible light spectrum; Thar & Bhm (2004) proposed biophotons as a neural signaling mechanism. But no experiment has attempted to determine whether: (1) DMT increases sensitivity to biophoton signals; (2) the information content of DNA biophoton emissions could include pharmacological information; (3) the visual experiences of ayahuasca are related to biophoton detection. The proposed mechanism is experimentally accessible — it could be tested with current technology. It has not been. This is not because it has been disproven; it is because no research group has prioritized testing it.

Sources

  • Popp et al., Naturwissenschaften (1984)
  • Thar & Bhm, PNAS (2004)
  • Narby, The Cosmic Serpent (1998) — Chapter 12 on testability
Then (1979) — Plants of the Gods

The Psilocybin Pharmacopoeia: From Schultes's 91 Plants to Phase 3 Trials

Schultes and Hofmann documented psilocybin mushrooms as one of the most culturally significant groups of psychoactive plants in the Americas — used by Mazatec, Zapotec, Mixtec, and other Mesoamerican cultures in healing ceremonies. They provided the ethnobotanical and pharmacological framework; the clinical research infrastructure didn't exist.
confirmed
COMPASS Pathways COMP360 psilocybin has completed two Phase 3 trials: COMP005 (June 2025, n=233, TRD): -3.6 MADRS point advantage over placebo at Week 6, p<0.001; COMP006 (February 2026, n=255, TRD): -3.8 MADRS point advantage, p<0.001. NDA submission planned Q4 2026. Australian TGA approved psilocybin for TRD and MDMA for PTSD in February 2023 — the world's first regulated psychedelic therapy approval. Johns Hopkins has studied psilocybin across addiction, depression, end-of-life anxiety, and major depressive disorder with consistently positive results. The plant that Schultes documented in 1979 as a Mazatec ceremonial sacrament is about to receive FDA approval as a treatment for treatment-resistant depression. The ethnobotanical documentation preceded the clinical development by 47 years.

Sources

  • COMPASS Pathways COMP005/COMP006 Phase 3 data (2025-2026)
  • TGA psilocybin approval (February 2023)
  • Griffiths et al. psilocybin studies (2006-2022)
Then (2001) — Plants of the Gods

The Schultes Students: Did the Next Generation Continue His Work?

Schultes spent decades training ethnobotanists at Harvard who would extend his documentation into the 21st century. He died in 2001, fourteen years before the psychedelic research renaissance he had hoped to see and not long enough after legalization to see the pharmaceutical development he had anticipated.
partially-confirmed
Schultes's students have collectively: published thousands of ethnobotanical papers; founded or directed the Ethnobotany Program at the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew (William Milliken); produced major popularizations of ethnobotany (Wade Davis's The Serpent and the Rainbow and One River; Mark Plotkin's Tales of a Shaman's Apprentice and The Amazon); co-founded the Heffter Research Institute (Dennis McKenna); established conservation programs for threatened medicinal plant knowledge in multiple countries; testified before Congress on indigenous rights. The School of Ethnobiology and Ethnoecology of Latin America (founded 1992) and multiple university ethnobotany programs trace directly to Schultes's framework. His work has been extended by a generation of researchers.

Sources

  • Davis, One River (1996)
  • Plotkin, Tales of a Shaman's Apprentice (1993)
  • McKenna, Heffter Research Institute (1993)
Then (1979) — Plants of the Gods

Ibogaine's Clinical Translation: Schultes's African Documentation Becoming Treatment

Schultes documented Tabernanthe iboga and its use in Bwiti initiation ceremonies in Central Africa — one of the most intensive psychoactive plant experiences documented anywhere. He could not have anticipated that 47 years later, ibogaine would be the focus of a $50 million state research program for veterans.
partially-confirmed
Ibogaine is now at the most advanced point in its clinical trajectory: Stanford study (Cherian et al., Nature Medicine, 2023, n=30 veterans): single ibogaine treatment produced significant reductions in PTSD (48% reduction), depression (42% reduction), anxiety (51% reduction), and disability ratings — maintained at 1-month follow-up. Texas HB 1893 (2025): $50 million for ibogaine research. Mississippi ibogaine research legislation (March 2026). Multiple Phase 2 trials ongoing (NYU, UCSF). The Bwiti ceremony documentation that Schultes contributed to is the provenance of the compound that could be the first psychedelic approved for PTSD and opioid use disorder. The ethnobotanical documentation preceded the clinical development by 47 years.

Sources

  • Cherian et al., Nature Medicine (2023)
  • Texas HB 1893 (2025)
  • Multidisciplinary ibogaine clinical trial network (2026)
Then (1979) — Plants of the Gods

The Language Loss Crisis: Schultes's Warning at Acceleration

Schultes's most urgent claim: indigenous botanical knowledge was disappearing faster than it could be documented, because it was encoded in languages and transmission systems that were dying faster than researchers could record them.
contested
Approximately 7,000 languages are spoken today. UNESCO estimates that by 2100, approximately 50-90% will be extinct. The Amazon alone: approximately 300 distinct indigenous languages spoken at the time of Schultes's fieldwork; approximately 150-180 survive with communities of active speakers today. Each language extinction represents the permanent loss of unique botanical vocabulary — plant names, preparation instructions, contraindications, combination knowledge — that has no written record. The Amazon Forest: 17% deforestation since 2000 (Brazil). Language loss and forest loss are correlated: indigenous territories with secure legal status have significantly lower deforestation rates. Schultes's warning has been confirmed; the crisis has exceeded his predictions in pace if not in direction.

Sources

  • UNESCO Atlas of World Languages in Danger (2010, 2022 update)
  • ISA-FUNAI indigenous territory deforestation studies (2024)
  • Terralingua Biocultural Diversity assessment (2023)
Then (1979) — Plants of the Gods

The Peyote Supply Problem: Can Indigenous Ceremony Be Sustained?

Schultes documented the Huichol peyote pilgrimage in detail — the ceremonies, the harvesting protocols, the cultural significance. He observed that peyote cultivation for ceremonial use required specific knowledge and specific conditions. He did not anticipate the conservation crisis that would develop as demand grew and habitat shrank.
contested
The Native American Church serves 250,000-500,000 members who use peyote ceremonially. Peyote grows in a small geographic range (Chihuahuan Desert of southern Texas and northern Mexico). The population has declined by an estimated 30%+ since the 1970s due to: habitat conversion to agriculture and ranching; overharvesting by unlicensed collectors; climate change reducing germination rates; slow growth rate (10-20 years to harvestable size). The NAC has formally requested exclusion from psychedelic decriminalization measures because any expansion of non-Native access would exacerbate the supply crisis. Colorado's Proposition 122 honored this request. Multiple NAC-affiliated cultivation projects are underway; they are producing a fraction of the needed supply. The culture Schultes documented may face extinction from supply collapse regardless of legal status.

Sources

  • Cactus Conservation Institute peyote population monitoring (2024)
  • NAC Conservation Statement (2023)
  • Colorado Prop 122 peyote exemption provisions

10 Cards Published

Flashcards

Study prompts for review — not a substitute for source checking. Citations appear only where present; question and answer are both printed below. 563 cards are held in the ledger; the rest are withheld until each carries an item-level source.

QuestionAnswerLevel
What is the primary mechanism of action of classical psychedelics?
mechanism
Agonist or partial agonist action at serotonin 5-HT2A receptors. This is the consensus mechanism. Glutamate signaling in the prefrontal cortex plays a significant secondary role. Neither serotonin flood nor dopamine — 5-HT2A is the key target.
Nichols, D.E. Pharmacological Reviews 68(2):264-355 (2016)
basic
What is functional selectivity at the 5-HT2A receptor and why does it matter therapeutically?
mechanism
The 5-HT2A receptor can activate two different downstream pathways: Gq protein (associated with psychedelic effects) and β-arrestin (associated with non-hallucinogenic effects). Drugs that selectively activate one pathway produce different effects — non-hallucinogenic 5-HT2A agonists (e.g., tabernanthalog) may produce therapeutic benefits without the psychedelic experience. This is the basis for second-generation psychedelic drug development.
Nichols, D.E. Pharmacological Reviews 68(2) (2016)
advanced
Where in the brain are 5-HT2A receptors most densely expressed?
brain-regions
Cortex (prefrontal, cingulate, parietal) — highest density, cognitive/perceptual effects. Thalamus and reticular nucleus — sensory gating. Primary visual cortex (V1) — explains visual phenomena. Raphe nuclei — serotonin production center. Locus coeruleus — alertness/arousal. Amygdala — emotion, fear and awe. Claustrum — proposed consciousness integrator, possible site of ego dissolution.
Nichols, D.E. Pharmacological Reviews 68(2) (2016)
intermediate
What is the safety profile of classical psychedelics?
safety
No established physiological lethal dose for LSD, psilocybin, DMT, or mescaline. No physical dependence. Rapid tolerance (cross-tolerance between 5-HT2A agonists) prevents consecutive-day use. HPPD (Hallucinogen Persisting Perception Disorder): rare, mechanism unclear, usually mild. NBOMe compounds are NOT classical psychedelics — they are full agonists with cardiovascular toxicity and have caused deaths. Do not conflate.
Nichols (2016); Weil & Rosen (1993) cited in Tupper (2003)
basic
What does psilocybin do to dendritic spines?
neuroplasticity
Psilocybin promotes dendritic spine growth in mouse frontal cortex, with the effect persisting for at least one month after a single dose. This is distinct from the acute 5-HT2A mechanism and involves intracellular receptor signaling. The neuroplasticity finding is one of the most significant recent developments in psychedelic neuroscience and may explain lasting therapeutic effects.
Shao et al. (2021); Vargas et al. (2023)
intermediate
What is the Default Mode Network and what do psychedelics do to it?
mechanism
The DMN is a set of brain regions active during self-referential thought, mind-wandering, and autobiographical memory. Hyperactivity is associated with depression and rumination. Psychedelics suppress DMN connectivity — particularly the medial prefrontal cortex and posterior cingulate — which correlates with ego dissolution and may explain anti-depressant effects by interrupting negative rumination loops.
Nichols (2016); Carhart-Harris et al. (multiple)
intermediate
What is the pharmacology of ayahuasca? Why does oral DMT work in ayahuasca but not on its own?
pharmacology
Ayahuasca = DMT (from Psychotria viridis or other admixture plants) + beta-carbolines (harmine, harmaline, tetrahydroharmine) from Banisteriopsis caapi. Beta-carbolines are MAO-A inhibitors — they block the gut and liver enzymes that would otherwise metabolize DMT before it reaches the brain. Without the MAOI, oral DMT is fully inactive. Additionally: harmine independently inhibits DYRK1A kinase, promoting neurogenesis through a separate pathway.
Labate & Cavnar, Therapeutic Use of Ayahuasca (2014); Labate & Cavnar, Ayahuasca Healing and Science (2021)
intermediate
What is endogenous DMT and what do we actually know about it?
pharmacology
CONFIRMED: DMT is present in human blood, urine, and cerebrospinal fluid — it is an endogenous compound produced by the same biochemical pathway as serotonin. UNCONFIRMED: The pineal gland as primary DMT production site (physiologically plausible, not demonstrated). UNCONFIRMED: That endogenous DMT produces psychedelic effects during dreams, near-death experiences, or meditation (interesting hypothesis, no measurement data). The physiological role of endogenous DMT remains unknown.
Nichols (2016); Roney-Dougal in Paranthropology Vol.2 No.2 (2011)
advanced
What therapeutic applications have the strongest evidence?
therapeutic
(1) Anxiety/depression in terminal illness — psilocybin, strong Phase 2 data (Hopkins, NYU). (2) Treatment-resistant depression — psilocybin, MDMA, Phase 2b/3 data. (3) PTSD — MDMA, MAPS Phase 3 (67% no longer meet diagnostic criteria post-treatment). (4) Alcohol/nicotine addiction — psilocybin, promising pilot data. (5) OCD — psilocybin, small trials. (6) Cluster headaches — patient self-report only, no trial data. MDMA note: MDMA is an entactogen, not a classical psychedelic — different mechanism, different patient population.
Nichols (2016); MAPS Phase 3 data; Gregoire, NEO.LIFE (2020)
intermediate
What is the "reducing valve" model and how does it map to current neuroscience?
mechanism
Huxley (1954), following Bergson: the brain normally narrows consciousness to what's relevant for survival, suppressing the rest. Mescaline removes this filter, allowing access to "Mind at Large." Current mapping: the Default Mode Network functions as a predictive filter, suppressing sensory inputs that confirm predictions. Psychedelics reduce DMN connectivity, allowing more raw sensory data through. Not an exact match — Huxley's model is optimistic (what's revealed is beautiful) while the neuroscience is neutral. The garden chair terror in Huxley's own account is the counterevidence his model doesn't fully account for.
Huxley (1954); Nichols (2016); Carhart-Harris et al.
intermediate

Claim Sorter Deck

58 claims taken from the books, each with the verdict, the reasoning, and the source it rests on. These are counted in the 454 published objects and used to be reachable only inside the Free University drill; they are printed here so they can be read, cited and checked. Open a claim to see the verdict — or read it cold first and sort it yourself.

The brain functions primarily as a reducing valve, filtering most of what could be perceived

Confirmed The Doors of Perception

The REBUS model (Carhart-Harris & Friston, 2019) formalizes this as 'precision weighting of top-down priors.' fMRI confirms DMN suppression under psychedelics. Huxley's 1954 metaphor maps precisely onto predictive coding theory.

Huxley, The Doors of Perception (1954) / Carhart-Harris & Friston (2019)

Psilocybin induces rapid and persistent growth of dendritic spines in frontal cortex

Confirmed Food of the Gods

Shao et al. (Yale, Neuron 2021): single psilocybin dose produces dendritic spine growth detectable at least one month later. Confirmed by multiple 2024-2025 studies. December 2025 Cell paper showed large-scale cortical network rewiring. Most robust neurobiological finding in current psychedelic research.

Shao et al., Neuron (2021); Zhao et al. (2024); Cell (2025)

The opposite of addiction is connection

Partially Confirmed Chasing the Scream

Social environment demonstrably modulates drug-seeking behavior (Rat Park, Vietnam). But Rat Park has not been directly replicated. Opioid withdrawal is a genuine physiological process. The 2023 fentanyl crisis (107,500 deaths) shows even connected people die from contaminated supply. The connection model is real but overstated.

Hari (2015); Gage & Sumnall, Addiction (2020); CDC (2023)

December 21, 2012 would be a singularity of maximum novelty — the Timewave Zero endpoint

Falsified True Hallucinations

The date passed without the predicted singularity or transformational event. McKenna had acknowledged the theory was falsifiable. The Timewave mathematics have been criticized by professional mathematicians. The underlying philosophical claim — that time has qualitative structure — is separable from the 2012 prediction and remains interesting; the specific prediction is falsified.

McKenna, True Hallucinations (1993); various commentaries 2012-2013

The Eleusinian Mysteries used an ergot-based psychedelic sacrament in the kykeon

Gaining Support The Road to Eleusis

Experimentally feasible (Antonopoulos & Dadiotis, Scientific Reports 2026 showed lye converts ergotamine to water-soluble psychoactive forms). Archaeologically evidenced at affiliated site (Mas Castellar de Pontós, 2019-2020). Direct confirmation at Eleusis itself — ergot residue in the Telesterion — has not yet been found. Moving from speculative to evidenced.

Wasson, Hofmann & Ruck (1978); Scientific Reports (2026)

Hemp prohibition in 1937 was orchestrated by DuPont and Hearst to eliminate hemp as competition

Partially Supported The Emperor Wears No Clothes

Corporate interests existed and benefited: DuPont's nylon patent (Feb 1938), Hearst's timber paper, the Mellon-Anslinger connection. But historians including Campos argue racial panic and moral reform were independently sufficient. DuPont benefited from prohibition; whether it orchestrated it is not conclusively proven. The scheduling was unjustified regardless.

Herer (1985); Campos, Home Grown (2012); WHO ECDD (2019)

Mystical experience quality predicts therapeutic outcomes better than drug dose alone

Confirmed LSD: My Problem Child

Confirmed across multiple conditions and institutions. Barrett & Griffiths (2018): MEQ30 score predicts sustained benefit in depression, AUD, end-of-life anxiety. Gukasyan et al. (2022): MEQ-outcome association persists at 12 months. COMPASS Phase 3 data consistent with mechanism. The therapeutic effect is mediated through the quality of experience, not only through pharmacology.

Barrett & Griffiths (2018); Gukasyan et al. (2022); Viljoen et al. (2025)

Set and setting (mindset and environment) are primary determinants of psychedelic outcomes

Confirmed Moksha: Letters of Huxley & Osmond

A 2024 Borkel et al. systematic review confirmed set and setting variables predict psychopathology, wellbeing, and meaningfulness across independent samples. Thal & Lommen (2024) meta-analysis of 75 clinical trials: therapeutic alliance, preparation, and integration quality are significant outcome predictors. Johnson et al. safety guidelines (2008) are now mandatory protocol for all clinical trials.

Borkel et al. (2024); Thal & Lommen (2024); Johnson et al. (2008)

Psilocybin-containing mushrooms catalyzed human cognitive evolution through regular consumption by early hominids

Unresolved Food of the Gods

No archaeological evidence of psilocybin use by early hominids. Psilocybe cubensis not documented in East Africa during the critical period. The neuroplasticity mechanism is real (Shao 2021). The broad question — what role did psychoactive plants play in human evolution? — is genuine and uninvestigated. The specific stoned ape timeline and mechanism are unsupported.

McKenna (1992); Shao et al. (2021); Wikipedia, Stoned Ape Theory

Shamans access molecular-level information (specifically DNA) through ayahuasca visions

Unresolved The Cosmic Serpent

The biophoton hypothesis is untested in relation to shamanic vision. Plant intelligence (Simard, Gagliano) and the combinatorial problem are real. The specific DNA-serpent-biophoton mechanism has not been tested experimentally. Narby's epistemological challenge — that 'we don't know how' ≠ 'it didn't happen' — is correct. The hypothesis generates testable predictions that have not been tested.

Narby (1998); Simard (2021); Gagliano et al. (2014)

The 1968 Schedule I classification of LSD was a scientific judgment based on evidence of harm

Falsified Storming Heaven

WHO Critical Review (2019) found no evidence supporting LSD's current scheduling level. FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation for psilocybin (2018) acknowledged classical psychedelics may have accepted medical use. Global Drug Survey 2016: LSD had lowest emergency medical treatment rate of any surveyed substance. Zero overdose deaths from LSD toxicity documented in 80 years. The scheduling was political.

Stevens (1987); WHO ECDD (2019); FDA (2018)

The machine elves McKenna described are consistently encountered by DMT users across cultures

Phenomenologically Confirmed True Hallucinations

Davis et al. 2020 (Johns Hopkins, J. Psychopharmacol. 34(9):1008-1020, n=2,561): respondents recruited for having had a DMT entity encounter described the entity as conscious, intelligent and benevolent; 69% reported receiving a message. The survey sampled people who had already had an encounter, so it does not establish a prevalence rate. Timmermann et al. 2023 (PNAS 120(13)): DMT produced large increases in global functional connectivity and a breakdown of network segregation; the study did not isolate entity contact. The consistency of the report is established; the explanation (unconscious projection vs. external encounter) is not.

Sexton et al., J. Psychopharmacol. 33(9) (2019); Timmermann et al. (2023)

Cannabis's Schedule I status has no accepted medical use — the scheduling criterion is met

Falsified The Emperor Wears No Clothes

WHO ECDD (2019) recommended cannabis reclassification, finding no scientific justification for Schedule I. FDA has approved Epidiolex (CBD), Syndros, Marinol, Cesamet (cannabinoid pharmaceuticals). DOJ proposed rescheduling to Schedule III (May 2024). 38 states have medical cannabis programs. The 'no accepted medical use' criterion is contradicted by FDA's own approval record.

Herer (1985); WHO ECDD (2019); FDA approvals

The drug war's racial targeting was incidental — an unintended consequence of neutral enforcement

Falsified Chasing the Scream

Ehrlichman (Nixon domestic policy adviser, Harper's 2016): 'We knew we couldn't make it illegal to be either against the war or Black, but...by criminalizing both heavily, we could disrupt those communities.' ACLU (2020): Black Americans 3.73x more likely to be arrested for marijuana despite similar use rates. The racial targeting was explicit policy, not incidental outcome.

Ehrlichman in Baum (2016); ACLU (2020)

Schultes's urgency about ethnopharmacological research was premature — there is still time

Falsified Plants of the Gods

Amazon has lost ~20% forest cover since Schultes's 1967 warning. Estimated one language (primary ethnobotanical knowledge carrier) lost every two weeks globally. Many plants Schultes documented are locally absent or rarer. The Kunming-Montreal Framework (2022) represents increased institutional response, but the race he described is still being lost at macro scale.

Schultes (1967); INPA (2023); CBD Kunming-Montreal (2022)

Portugal's drug decriminalization model is a straightforward success that any country could replicate

Partially Supported Chasing the Scream

Portugal's results through 2015 were strong (HIV transmission down ~95%, overdose deaths down). Results 2015-2023 were weaker as austerity cut social service programs. Oregon's Measure 110 decriminalization was repealed in 2024 due to implementation failures. The lesson: decriminalization + social investment works; decriminalization alone is insufficient. The model works under specific conditions.

Hari (2015); EMCDDA (2023); Wikipedia, Oregon Measure 110

Hofmann's LSD is best understood as a 'sacred drug' rather than a psychiatric tool

Gaining Clinical Support LSD: My Problem Child

Clinical evidence supports the 'mechanism through sacred/mystical experience' hypothesis: MEQ30 scores predict outcomes, mystical experience quality mediates therapeutic benefit. But 'sacred' remains outside clinical vocabulary. COMPASS Pathways describes COMP360 as 'a drug with psychedelic properties.' The phenomenological claim (it works through a quality of experience humans have called sacred) is supported; the ontological claim (it is sacred) is not clinically testable.

Hofmann (1979); Barrett & Griffiths (2018); COMPASS (2026)

Television is a dominator drug that produces passivity and compliance

More Accurate Now Than When Written Food of the Gods

McKenna wrote this in 1992 about network TV. Sean Parker (2017): Facebook was 'designed to exploit psychological vulnerabilities.' Haidt (2024): smartphone social media correlates with dramatic increases in adolescent depression/anxiety. The algorithmic feed is a more effective version of what McKenna described — variable-ratio reinforcement, individual optimization, infinite scroll. The mechanism he identified is real; the technology has become much more powerful.

McKenna (1992); Parker interview (2017); Haidt, The Anxious Generation (2024)

Plato's theory of Forms was influenced by his Eleusinian initiation

Unresolved The Road to Eleusis

Plato was historically confirmed as an Eleusinian initiate. The phenomenological parallel between the Allegory of the Cave and psychedelic mystical experience is striking. Classical scholars (Burkert) argue theatrical performance was sufficient; Ruck argues the 'vision' language requires pharmacological explanation. The hypothesis is philosophically coherent but not falsifiable with available evidence.

Wasson, Hofmann & Ruck (1978); Burkert (1987); Muraresku (2020)

Huxley's mescaline experience was a 'gratuitous grace' — potentially valuable but not necessary for enlightenment

Confirmed (By Clinical Evidence) The Doors of Perception

Current clinical evidence supports this framing exactly. Psilocybin reliably produces mystical experience (MEQ30) in appropriate conditions — but mystical experience can also be produced by meditation, near-death experience, and other non-pharmacological means. The drug is a reliable tool, not the only path. Huxley's qualifier — 'not necessary, potentially helpful' — maps precisely onto how clinical researchers understand the compound's role.

Huxley (1954); Griffiths et al. (2006); Yaden & Griffiths (2021)

The Eleusinian Mysteries were a theatrical experience — no pharmacological agent was required to produce the described visions

Unresolved The Road to Eleusis

Walter Burkert, the leading scholar of ancient Greek religion, argued that theatrical performance, psychological suggestion, and the powerful ritual context were sufficient. The Road to Eleusis hypothesis argues the consistent testimony of 'vision' (not 'emotion') language across five centuries requires a pharmacological explanation. The Mas Castellar de Pontós findings (2019-2020) provide physical evidence of ergot at an affiliated site. Direct testing at Eleusis has not been done. Both positions remain arguable from the available evidence.

Burkert (1987); Wasson, Hofmann & Ruck (1978); Juan-Tresserras (2019-2020)

FDA approval of psilocybin-assisted therapy would make it broadly accessible to patients who need it

Probably False LSD: My Problem Child

The Australian experience after the world's first psychedelic therapy approval (February 2023) is the most relevant data point: treatment costs $25,000-35,000 AUD per patient with no insurance coverage, fewer than 100 psychiatrists authorized nationally by mid-2024, access almost exclusively to wealthy private patients. US approval without mandatory insurance coverage and reimbursement would produce a similar boutique market. Approval is necessary but not sufficient for broad access.

TGA Australia (2023); Australian Healthcare & Hospitals Association (2025)

The psychedelic renaissance represents a genuine cultural shift — an Archaic Revival in McKenna's sense

Contested Food of the Gods

Evidence for: legal psilocybin services, bipartisan political support, FDA Breakthrough Therapy designations, clinical research renaissance. Evidence against: dominant engagement mode is consumer wellness (branded microdosing, $500 retreats, Silicon Valley productivity optimization). McKenna's Archaic Revival was specifically about cultural reorientation toward plant intelligence and indigenous knowledge — not a new pharmaceutical category. The dominant commercial form is arguably the dominator culture adapting to a new market rather than being transformed by it.

McKenna (1992); MAPS Policy Guidebook (2026); Colorado Sun (2025)

Ibogaine is the most promising psychedelic for treating opioid use disorder and PTSD in veterans

Promising, Evidence Still Early Food of the Gods

Small studies showing dramatic results: Noller et al. 2018 (n=14 OUD): 69% reduction in withdrawal symptoms. Stanford Kirchner et al. 2023 (n=30 veterans): significant reductions in PTSD, depression, disability. Texas allocated $50M for ibogaine research in 2025, Mississippi passed ibogaine research bill March 2026. BUT: ibogaine has cardiac risks (QTc prolongation) that have caused deaths; no Phase 3 RCT has been completed; no FDA approval pathway established. Evidence is compelling enough to fund large trials; not strong enough to establish clinical efficacy.

Noller et al. (2018); Kirchner et al. (2023); High Times (April 2026)

The mescaline experience produces genuine mystical states identical to those described by contemplative mystics

Confirmed (MEQ30) The Doors of Perception

Pahnke's Good Friday Experiment (1962) and subsequent studies using the MEQ30 show that psilocybin (structurally similar mechanism) produces experiences meeting all six Stace mystical criteria. Griffiths et al. (2016) directly compared drug-induced and spontaneous mystical experiences — rated equivalently. The phenomenological identity Huxley claimed is confirmed; whether transformation is equivalent remains open.

Psychedelic education should be integrated into mainstream curricula — 'consciousness literacy'

Gaining Institutional Traction The Doors of Perception

Johns Hopkins Center for Psychedelic Research (2019) and Imperial College London Centre for Psychedelic Research (2019) offer graduate-level training. MAPS Public Benefit Corporation runs therapist certification programs. The American Psychiatric Association has added psychedelic-related CME sessions. The proposal remains far from K-12 or undergraduate implementation, but it is in medical and graduate curricula.

Art functions as 'ersatz suchness' — a substitute for the direct visionary experience that most people cannot access

Partially Confirmed The Doors of Perception

Consistent with psychological research showing that aesthetic experience activates networks overlapping with psychedelic experience (Vessel et al., Frontiers in Human Neuroscience, 2012). Brain imaging confirms art-induced awe shares neural features with ego dissolution. But Huxley's claim is not primarily empirical — it is philosophical. As a philosophical claim about art's function, it is neither confirmed nor falsified.

A guided psychedelic session can produce lasting change in personality traits — specifically increases in openness

Confirmed Moksha: Letters of Huxley & Osmond

MacLean, Johnson & Griffiths (Psychopharmacology, 2011): single psilocybin session produced lasting increases in the trait 'openness to experience' (one of the Big Five personality traits) — a trait typically stable in adults after age 30. The change persisted at 14-month follow-up. This is the first demonstration of psychedelic-induced lasting personality change. Consistent with Huxley and Osmond's clinical observations.

The physical setting of a psychedelic session should be aesthetically comfortable and carefully prepared

Confirmed (Empirical) Moksha: Letters of Huxley & Osmond

Borkel et al. (2024, systematic review): setting variables — room aesthetics, music, therapist relational style — collectively account for significant variance in outcomes, independent of drug dose. The MAPS and COMPASS protocols both specify detailed setting requirements. The FDA's concerns about the Lykos NDA included inadequate attention to setting standardization.

LSD-assisted psychotherapy can achieve lasting sobriety in alcoholism at rates exceeding other available treatments

Confirmed (Historical + Modern) Moksha: Letters of Huxley & Osmond

Krebs & Johansen meta-analysis (Journal of Psychopharmacology, 2012): six RCTs from the original Hoffer-Osmond program showing statistically significant effects on alcohol misuse at 6-month follow-up. Bogenschutz et al. (JAMA Psychiatry, 2022): psilocybin for alcohol use disorder — 83% reduction in heavy drinking days. The clinical finding Osmond made in Saskatchewan in 1952 has been replicated 70 years later with a structurally similar compound.

LSD is not addictive in the conventional sense — it does not produce physical dependence or compulsive use patterns

Confirmed LSD: My Problem Child

No evidence of physical dependence (withdrawal syndrome on cessation). Rapid tolerance development means compulsive daily use is self-limiting. Population surveys (Global Drug Survey) consistently find LSD at the bottom of addiction rankings. The WHO ECDD (2019) found no evidence supporting current scheduling on addiction grounds. DEA's own scheduling data: LSD has the lowest abuse potential per capita of scheduled substances.

LSD microdosing (sub-perceptual doses) produces measurable cognitive benefits

Contested LSD: My Problem Child

The microdosing literature is genuinely mixed. Szigeti et al. (eLife, 2021): a self-blinded RCT found microdosing produced expected effects (reduced depression, anxiety) in the open label phase — but also in the placebo phase. Active vs placebo difference: not significant. Anderson et al. (Journal of Psychopharmacology, 2019): observational study found positive self-reported effects. Most microdosing research has methodological problems (expectancy effects, self-selection). The claim is not confirmed and not refuted.

A single psilocybin session can produce lasting reduction in tobacco addiction

Confirmed (Phase 2) LSD: My Problem Child

Johnson et al. (Drug and Alcohol Dependence, 2014): psilocybin-assisted therapy produced 80% abstinence at 6-month follow-up in a sample of long-term smokers who had failed multiple previous quit attempts. This is the highest documented cessation rate for any smoking treatment. Garcia-Romeu et al. follow-up (2014): 60% abstinence at 12 months. Phase 2 RCT underway at Johns Hopkins. The finding supports Hofmann's claim that single sessions can produce lasting change.

Psilocybin increases nature connectedness and pro-environmental attitudes

Confirmed Food of the Gods

Lyons & Carhart-Harris (Psychopharmacology, 2018): psilocybin significantly increased nature relatedness scores; this increase correlated with reduced authoritarian political attitudes. Forstmann & Sagioglou (Frontiers in Psychology, 2021): lifetime psychedelic use predicted greater nature connectedness and pro-environmental behavior, independent of political orientation. Kettner et al. (2019) confirmed the connectedness effect naturalistically. McKenna's ecological argument — that plant medicines teach kinship with nature — has measurable correlates.

The human drive to alter consciousness is as fundamental as hunger or sex

Supported But Not Proven Food of the Gods

Andrew Weil made this argument in The Natural Mind (1972); McKenna reinforced it. Evidence: virtually every human culture across history has used consciousness-altering substances; children spontaneously spin to induce dizziness; religious practices universally seek altered states. No neuroscientific study has established a specific 'altered consciousness drive' analogous to hunger's homeostatic mechanism. The cross-cultural universality is well-documented; the specific neurological mechanism is not established.

Social media platforms are designed to exploit psychological vulnerabilities in ways that structurally resemble addictive drug use

Confirmed (By Designer Admission) Food of the Gods

Sean Parker (founding president of Facebook) stated in 2017: 'How do we consume as much of your time and conscious attention as possible? ... We give you a little dopamine hit every once in a while.' Tristan Harris (former Google design ethicist) documented persuasive technology design in The Social Dilemma (2020). Haidt's The Anxious Generation (2024) documented correlations between smartphone social media adoption and adolescent mental health decline. McKenna's 1992 argument about television as dominator drug applies with greater precision to social media.

Drug prohibition increases violence by creating black markets with no legal dispute resolution

Confirmed (Historical Evidence) Chasing the Scream

The pattern is documented in two natural experiments: US alcohol Prohibition (1920-1933) produced gang violence over bootlegging territory; Prohibition repeal eliminated this violence. The drug war in Mexico, Central America, and US inner cities produced cartel warfare over supply routes valued by prohibition-created profit margins. Miron (2004, The Budgetary Implications of Marijuana Prohibition) estimated prohibition-related violence costs. The mechanism: legal markets resolve disputes through contracts and courts; illegal markets resolve them through violence.

Drug addiction is primarily a response to trauma, not primarily a pharmacological inevitability

Substantially Supported Chasing the Scream

ACE Study (Felitti et al., 1998): dose-response relationship between adverse childhood experiences and addiction risk. Rat Park (Alexander et al., 1978-1981): environment substantially modulates addiction. Vietnam natural experiment (Robins, 1972): 95% of regular heroin users quit without treatment upon return to social connection. But: opioid use disorder develops in approximately 8-12% of people prescribed opioids for pain, including those without trauma histories. Pharmacological factors are real; the claim that addiction is 'primarily' trauma-driven overstates what the evidence shows.

Cannabis legalization does not produce significant increases in youth cannabis use

Confirmed (US Data) Chasing the Scream

Monitoring the Future surveys (2012-2024): youth cannabis use in recreational cannabis states has not significantly increased post-legalization; in some age groups (8th grade), slight decreases. The SAMHSA National Survey on Drug Use and Health shows similar patterns nationally. The fear that legalization normalizes cannabis for youth — the primary argument against medical cannabis access in the 1990s — has not been borne out in a decade of legal state data.

The Eleusinian Mysteries at Eleusis used a pharmacologically active kykeon — some psychoactive preparation

Gaining Physical Evidence The Road to Eleusis

Mas Castellar de Pontós analysis (Egea et al., Antiquity, 2020): ergot alkaloids detected in dental calculus from a woman buried at a Demeter cult site; ergot spores found in sealed ritual vessels. Antonopoulos & Dadiotis (Scientific Reports, 2026): lye converts toxic ergot to psychoactive LSA derivatives under ancient conditions. Physical evidence exists at an affiliated site; direct analysis at Eleusis itself has not been conducted. The hypothesis has moved from speculative to evidenced.

Classical Greek philosophers including Plato underwent the Eleusinian initiation

Historically Confirmed The Road to Eleusis

Multiple ancient sources confirm: Plato describes experiences consistent with initiation language in the Phaedo and Phaedrus; Sophocles, Pindar, Cicero, Plutarch, and Marcus Aurelius are all historically documented as initiates. The initiation was open to all Greek-speakers and was the most common religious experience in the ancient Mediterranean world — millions were initiated over a thousand years. That specific named philosophers were initiates is confirmed by their own writings and by ancient historians.

Religious freedom law (RFRA) provides protection for sacramental use of Schedule I substances

Confirmed (SCOTUS) The Road to Eleusis

Gonzales v. O Centro Espirita Beneficente Uniao do Vegetal (SCOTUS, 2006): unanimous ruling that RFRA required the government to demonstrate a compelling interest by the least restrictive means before prohibiting UDV's sacramental hoasca (ayahuasca) use. Government failed to meet this standard. Subsequent lower court cases for ayahuasca, peyote, and psilocybin have applied O Centro with similar results. RFRA protection for sincere sacramental use of psychedelics is established law.

The 1968 LSD research program had a clinical evidence base sufficient for therapeutic application

Confirmed Retrospectively Storming Heaven

Krebs & Johansen (2012) retrospective meta-analysis of six RCTs from the original program showed statistically significant effects for alcoholism. Grof's end-of-life anxiety work at Maryland was replicated with similar effect sizes in the 2016 Johns Hopkins and NYU studies. The original research was not terminated for scientific failure — it produced results that modern replications confirm. What would have happened with 40 more years of research is unknowable, but the starting point was real.

The CIA's MK-Ultra LSD program was counterproductive to its stated goals

Confirmed Storming Heaven

Church Committee Investigation (1975): MK-Ultra produced no operational intelligence value from LSD. Subjects were uncontrollable; information obtained under LSD was unreliable; the drug could not produce the compliance the CIA sought. The program's only confirmed 'result' was Frank Olson's death and the contamination of the civilian research program with association to government malfeasance. The Church Committee report is the primary source. The CIA's own internal reviews (partially declassified) reached similar conclusions.

The psychedelic research program, if it had continued without the 1968 scheduling, would have produced FDA-approved treatments by the 1980s

Unknowable Counterfactual Storming Heaven

The research was producing positive results at rates comparable to what the 2016-2026 research program has produced. The methodological standards required for FDA approval in 1975 were different from current standards. Whether the existing evidence base would have been sufficient for NDA submission is unknowable. Jay Stevens argues it would have taken another 5-10 years of uninterrupted work. The claim is plausible but not verifiable.

Cannabis has no accepted medical use — the Schedule I criterion is met

Definitively Falsified The Emperor Wears No Clothes

Epidiolex (purified CBD) is FDA-approved for Dravet syndrome and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. Marinol and Syndros (synthetic THC) are Schedule III FDA-approved medications since 1985. 38 states have medical cannabis programs. The WHO ECDD (2019) explicitly recommended cannabis reclassification away from Schedule I, finding evidence of medical utility insufficient to justify current scheduling. The 'no accepted medical use' criterion has been factually inapplicable since at least 1985.

The 1937 Marihuana Tax Act was designed primarily to eliminate hemp as an industrial competitor

Circumstantially Supported The Emperor Wears No Clothes

The evidence: Hearst and DuPont had financial interests in suppressing hemp. The Act was passed with unusual speed, minimal testimony, and at a moment when hemp processing technology was becoming commercially viable. But: no documentary evidence of explicit coordination between Hearst, DuPont, and Anslinger. The 'DuPont memo' Herer cites is disputed in interpretation. Alternative explanation: racial and political motivations (Anslinger's documented racism, anti-immigration sentiment) are sufficient to explain the Act without industrial conspiracy. The conspiracy is plausible, not proven.

Industrial hemp can produce as much paper per acre as trees and with superior environmental impact

Confirmed Agronomically The Emperor Wears No Clothes

USDA Agricultural Research Service hemp fiber studies (2021): hemp yields 250% more fiber per acre than cotton; requires approximately 50% less water; requires minimal pesticide input. Environmental Life Cycle Assessment studies (European Industrial Hemp Association, 2022) show hemp paper has lower carbon footprint per ton than wood pulp paper across all categories except water use in some growing regions. The agronomic claims Herer made are confirmed. The commercial translation has not followed at the scale he predicted.

DMT entities are consistently reported across cultures, suggesting they are not purely culturally constructed

Phenomenologically Confirmed True Hallucinations

Davis et al. (2020, J. Psychopharmacol. 34(9), n=2,561 people who had had an entity encounter): descriptions consistent across cultures and demographics — 'beings of light,' 'elves/gnomes,' 'aliens,' 'guides.' No controlled imaging study has yet reported an entity-contact-specific neural signature; a 2021 Frontiers in Psychology study with n=39 has been cited for this and does not exist. The phenomenological consistency across cultural backgrounds is established. The interpretation — whether entities are neural artifacts, unconscious projections, or encountered independently — is not resolved by the consistency data.

The La Chorrera experiment of 1971 produced a genuine philosophical breakthrough

Contested and Unresolvable True Hallucinations

Terence McKenna claimed La Chorrera produced cosmological revelations. Dennis McKenna (Brotherhood of the Screaming Abyss, 2012) characterized the experience primarily as psychosis with philosophical overlay. The 'experiment' produced Timewave Zero — which was falsified in 2012. It also produced Terence's public career and Dennis's scientific career, both of which had significant real-world impact. Whether a 'genuine philosophical breakthrough' occurred depends on definitions that the two witnesses to the event disagree about.

High-dose psilocybin produces experiences indistinguishable from near-death experiences

Substantially Overlapping True Hallucinations

Martial et al. (Frontiers in Psychology, 2019): systematic comparison of NDE phenomenology and psychedelic experience phenomenology across 18 features — significant overlap in ego dissolution, ineffability, encounter with entities, sense of cosmic unity, time distortion. NDE survivors and psychedelic users rate the experiences as among the most meaningful of their lives on similar scales. Differences: NDEs more commonly include life review; psilocybin more commonly includes geometric visual phenomena. The overlap is substantial and meaningful; the experiences are not identical.

Amazonian peoples developed the ayahuasca combination through rational empirical observation rather than supernatural guidance

The Combinatorial Problem Remains Open The Cosmic Serpent

The standard scientific explanation — trial and error over thousands of years — is challenged by the mathematics of the combinatorial problem: 80,000 candidate species, two specific species whose interaction is not obvious, pharmacological interaction requiring understanding of MAO inhibition that wasn't formalized until 1952. Trial-and-error proponents: Schultes himself believed systematic empirical observation over millennia was sufficient. Narby's counter: the specific biochemical interaction is too counter-intuitive to discover by ingestion alone. The question remains genuinely open.

Plants communicate with each other through chemical and electrical signals in ecologically meaningful ways

Confirmed The Cosmic Serpent

Simard et al. (Nature, 1997): mycorrhizal network carbon and nutrient transfer. Baldwin et al. (Nature, 2001): tobacco plants release volatile signals (methyl jasmonate) that prime neighboring plants' defenses against herbivores. Karban et al. review (Ecology Letters, 2013): plant-plant volatile communication is documented across hundreds of species. Electrical signaling through mycorrhizal networks: Bhm et al. (Plant Signaling & Behavior, 2016). The existence of plant communication is established across multiple mechanisms. Narby's claim that plants 'communicate' is confirmed; his specific mechanism (biophoton-DMT) has not been tested.

The extraction of indigenous pharmacological knowledge without benefit-sharing constitutes biopiracy under international law

Confirmed By Treaty The Cosmic Serpent

The Nagoya Protocol (2010, in force 2014) defines misappropriation of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge without prior informed consent and benefit-sharing as a violation of international law. 143 states are parties. The ayahuasca patent case (US Patent 5751 to Loren Miller, challenged 1999) established the legal category in US law. Whether the psychedelic pharmaceutical industry's development of psilocybin, ibogaine, and mescaline derivatives from ethnobotanically-derived knowledge constitutes Nagoya-covered biopiracy is legally contested; the moral argument is established.

Every major plant-derived drug in the modern pharmacopoeia was first identified through ethnobotanical observation

Confirmed Plants of the Gods

Documented cases: quinine (malaria) from Cinchona — Quechua peoples; curare (muscle relaxant) from Strychnos/Chondrodendron — Amazonian peoples; aspirin from willow bark — multiple cultures; morphine from opium poppy — ancient Mediterranean and Asian cultures; taxol from Pacific yew — discovered through systematic screening of plants identified in ethnobotanical literature; artemisinin (malaria) from qinghao — Chinese traditional medicine. The pattern is universal. Newman & Cragg (Journal of Natural Products, 2020): approximately 50% of drugs approved 1981-2019 were natural product-derived.

The peyote conservation crisis will result in the extinction of traditional Native American Church ceremonies within this generation without intervention

Crisis-Level But Not Inevitable Plants of the Gods

The peyote population has declined 30%+ since the 1970s. Current harvest rates exceed estimated sustainable yield. The NAC membership is growing. Cultivation projects exist but produce a fraction of needed supply. The math is concerning: if trends continue, supply shortage will significantly impair ceremonial access within 20-30 years. But: cultivation technology is improving; habitat protection efforts are underway in Texas; synthetic mescaline research (which the NAC has not opposed) could reduce demand for natural peyote. The crisis is real; the outcome is not yet determined.

The ethnobotanical pharmacopoeia represents the most important untapped resource for new drug development

Confirmed by Track Record Plants of the Gods

Newman & Cragg (Journal of Natural Products, 2020): 50% of drugs approved 1981-2019 were natural product-derived or inspired. Ethnobotanically-guided drug discovery is approximately 30x more efficient than random screening (Fabricant & Farnsworth, Environmental Health Perspectives, 2001). Schultes's 91 plants have produced: psilocybin (approaching FDA approval), ibogaine (Phase 2 trials), mescaline (decriminalized in Colorado), DMT/ayahuasca (Phase 2 trials), multiple non-psychedelic therapeutic leads. The pharmacological resource Schultes documented is far from exhausted.

Ibogaine is the most effective single-session treatment for opioid use disorder currently known

Promising but Phase 2 Only Plants of the Gods

Stanford study (Cherian et al., Nature Medicine, 2023, n=30 veterans): 48% reduction in PTSD, 42% depression, 51% anxiety at 1-month follow-up. Multiple observational studies at ibogaine clinics in Mexico show 50-70% opioid abstinence at 1-year follow-up in heavily treatment-resistant populations. But: no Phase 3 RCT has been completed; cardiac safety (ibogaine prolongs QT interval) requires controlled administration; the comparison is to a very poorly-performing field (standard OUD treatment has <30% long-term remission). The claim may be true; the evidence base is Phase 2.
